The registry attributes to it 'OpenCascade valid-solid/re-import/bounding-box/volume checks' under a 'CAD exchange/solid-modeling background' equation_ref. Grep for opencascade, occ, solid, topolog, b-rep/brep, boundary, STEP, IGES, exchange, bounding, volume, valid, manifold, shell, edge, vertex, euler, kernel, export returned zero relevant hits ('import' matches only unrelated text; 'closed' refers to closed curves; 'tolerance' appears once in a control-point replacement step). The document contains no solid-modeling, topology-validity, data-exchange, re-import, bounding-box or volume-check content, so it cannot support the model. The only tangentially related geometric statement is the convex-hull containment property of B-spline curves (page 40), which is a curve property, not a kernel verification policy.

models.current_support_note: Original White PDF pp840-842 recovers Eq7.42 delta/x approx0.16 Re_x^(-1/7) and Eq7.46 delta_star approxdelta/8, implying0.02 x Re_x^(-1/7). This is a smooth flat-plate derivation using a one-seventh-power profile and constant outer velocity. The implementation instead uses0.046*s/Re_s^(1/5)*sqrt(max(T/T_wall,0.2)), with local nozzle properties, distance since throat, radius floor and blockage clipping. The coefficient, exponent, temperature factor, floors/clips and nozzle application are repository screening assumptions, not established by these source equations. No justified substitution of the flat-plate formula into the nozzle is made. CITES links explicitly connect the compared source equations without asserting IMPLEMENTS; numerical validity of the nozzle extension and physical calibration remain unavailable.

models.current_support_note: SP-125 (the registry's local source) prints Nu = C1 Re^0.8 Pr^0.4 (mu/mu_w)^0.14 with a coolant-specific C1 (RP-1: 0.0214, PDF p.119). The code and registry use 0.027 Re^0.8 Pr^(1/3) (mu_b/mu_w)^0.14 (the classical Sieder & Tate 1936 form, which is not held in the corpus). Same structure and viscosity correction; different coefficient and Prandtl exponent. Relative to the SP-125 RP-1 form the code's h_c is higher by about 26% at Pr = 1, 17% at Pr = 3 and 7% at Pr = 11.7 (RP-1 at 600 R).
